speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We had originally wanted the Motion statement to state that the suspension would be: (a) until Minister Iswaran has been cleared of all wrongdoing and he is able to resume duties or (b) until the end of the current session of the 14th Parliament, whichever is earlier.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We were, however, advised by Parliamentary staff that the first condition is not sufficiently definite and thus cannot form part of the Motion statement.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We had also originally wanted the Motion statement to include the provision that should Minister Iswaran be cleared of all wrongdoing, the Member of Parliament's (MP) allowance not paid over the duration of the suspension should then be paid to him.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We were informed that this also cannot form part of the Motion statement because, currently, the law does not allow that to be done.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If we wish to back pay Minister Iswaran, legislative changes will have to be made.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is why we have also asked for leave to introduce a Bill to make that possible.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The main goal of my Private Member's Bill is to empower Parliament to authorise the back payment of the allowance of an MP who has been suspended from the service of Parliament by resolution.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thus, the Motion statement stands as it is today.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is the first time since Independence that such a Motion has been moved in this House.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My colleague, Mr Leong Mun Wai and I have placed this Motion before the House after serious consideration.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is not a case of "Anything you can do, I can do stronger", as the Prime Minister said during the Sitting on 2 August.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since 12 July, Minister Iswaran has been instructed by the Prime Minister to take leave of absence from his official duties until the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) completes its investigations into him.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Prime Minister said that it was not within his discretion to cut the MP allowance.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Hence, the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) decided to file the Motion to suspend Minister Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How is this case different from others as to warrant a suspension?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Prime Minister has made the decision to place Minister Iswaran on leave of absence in both his capacity as Minister as well as MP.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While we do not have the details of the investigation that the Prime Minister is privy to, we believe the Prime Minister must have good reasons to do so.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, in effect, Minister Iswaran has been fully suspended from his MP duties, but not from his MP allowance.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We believe this merits a strong statement that reflects our values.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In addition, for many years, the Government has justified the high salaries for political officeholders on the basis of ensuring that our Government remains honest and free of corruption.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is why many Singaporeans, including myself, find it difficult to accept that taxpayers' money is being used in this way.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us set aside this particular case involving Minister Iswaran for the time being and instead, consider a generic case of corruption.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Should we have a system that allows an outcome whereby an MP who is eventually found guilty of corruption and whose duties had been suspended can continue to receive in full his or her MP allowance over the entire duration of the investigation plus the duration of Court proceedings until he or she is finally pronounced guilty, and all avenues of appeal exhausted?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is this a good use of tax revenue?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is this not a drain on our resources?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this is not a desirable outcome, then we need to do something.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This Motion is therefore about the prudent use of taxpayers' money, not a presumption of guilt.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While we do not want corrupt MPs to benefit financially, we must balance that with ensuring that innocent MPs do not have to pay a price for accusations or suspicions that are later proved unfounded.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To do that, we have two options: the first is to pay the allowance first and then claw back if found guilty; the second is to suspend the allowance and then pay back if found innocent.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Both of these options are currently not legal.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Existing laws do not allow any clawback of allowance nor paying back of withheld allowance.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Legislative changes are necessary to adopt either one.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under the first option of 'pay first, claw back later", a potential problem exists.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: After the payment of the allowance, we have no control over where the money flows.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There might be difficulties later in recovering the sum of money; and time, effort and cost may be incurred in the recovery.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Leader of the House has also filed a Motion today.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are three parts to the Motion, which I would deal with in turn.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clause (a) of the Leader's Motion asked the House to affirm the need for MPs to uphold the highest standards of integrity and conduct themselves in accordance with the law.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are also of the belief that MPs have a responsibility to be men and women of integrity and to act in accordance with the law.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is our duty to Singaporeans and what Singaporeans expect of us.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clause (b) of the Leader's Motion asked the House to affirm the need to deal firmly and fairly with any MP who is being investigated for possible wrongdoing.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In principle, PSP has no objection to this.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, we may differ on what constitutes "firmly" and "fairly".

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are not advocating that any MP who is under investigation should be suspended.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That would indeed be unfair and setting the bar too low.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Anyone can lodge a complaint and an investigation will be triggered.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clause (c) of the Leader's Motion asked the House to resolve to consider the matter regarding Minister Iswaran when the outcome of the ongoing investigation against him is known.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In effect, it is asking the House to maintain the status quo where Minister Iswaran continues to draw his MP allowance until the investigations against him are completed.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is unclear how long the investigations will take.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have seen that corruption investigations can take a long time, especially when it involves overseas participants.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In 2017, Keppel Offshore & Marine (KOM) admitted to corruption to the US Department of Justice.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If we do not suspend Minister Iswaran and he is subsequently charged and found guilty of corruption, we would not be able to recover the allowances that were paid to him while he was under investigation and not performing his duties.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There have been precedents of MPs who have remained an MP and continued to draw the full MP allowance throughout the entire legal process while they were charged for corruption until they chose to resign or were otherwise disqualified from office.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This was the case with former PAP MP and Minister of State Wee Toon Boon in the 1970s, who remained an MP throughout his trial for corruption.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He was charged in April 1975 for corruption.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He remained an MP for another one year and five months until September 1976 when he resigned.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: By the time he resigned as an MP, he had already served two months of his 18-month jail term.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP believes that it would be a most unsatisfactory situation if this were to happen in the case of Minister Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That is why today I have moved this Motion and sought leave to table a Private Member's Bill to amend the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act in order to create the legal mechanisms to back pay an MP their allowance if they are suspended.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP believes that the suspension together with the provision to back pay him should he be cleared of all wrongdoing is indeed dealing with the matter firmly and fairly.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Motion moved by the Leader of the House does not achieve this.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is, in fact, calling for a maintenance of the status quo.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us compare the financial outcome of suspending Minister Iswaran versus not suspending under two scenarios of him being innocent or guilty.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If Minister Iswaran is innocent, there is no difference in outcome between suspending or not suspending him.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, if Minister Iswaran is found guilty, there is a distinct difference.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If he is not suspended from Parliament, he will gain the MP allowance while taxpayers lose tax revenue.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If he is suspended, he loses the allowance while taxpayers save on tax revenue.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I hope all Members will support the Motion moved by Mr Leong Mun Wai and I.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I just wish to seek some clarifications from Ms Poa so that when I do my reply later, I can do so in a considered manner and we are not talking at cross purposes.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The first clarification I am seeking is this: under what specific provision is Ms Poa seeking to suspend Mr Iswaran?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I know Ms Poa would like to suspend him in order to cut his allowance.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But the cutting of the allowance is an outcome.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There has to be, as I mentioned in my earlier speech, a threshold, a section of legislation or some legal provision where you seek suspension.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, my clarification is this – under which section of legislation or what regulation is Ms Poa seeking to suspend?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Basically, it is a provision where there is no restriction to circumstances under which Parliament can suspend a Member.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Is Ms Poa referring to the Standing Orders (SOs)?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: My second clarification, therefore, is this – if that is the relevant provision of the SOs, is Ms Poa saying that we do not need to have any principles for suspension?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In other words, you do not look to see whether something has occurred; in other words, you do it because you can do it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What is the principle on which she is saying that we should suspend?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I believe I have stated the basis of asking for suspension quite clearly.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I accept that there are no current rules prescribing exactly the circumstances under which a Member can be suspended, but I do not see that as a prohibition against doing something that we feel is the right thing to do even though the rule has not yet been put in place.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because Ms Poa has limited it quite carefully to corruption.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Can I ask Ms Poa, is it her view then that if an MP is under investigation for murder or for rape, then suspension should not apply?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I have not thought about those other cases.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: It is not my intention to set out the rules under which Members can be suspended.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I am merely looking at the case in point, where I feel there is a strong case for suspension.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: As to setting out generic rules, I believe that there will be somebody in Government or Leader of the House that is in charge of that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Poa is not bringing this Motion as a matter of broad principle of general application, but a very specific targeted Motion directed at Mr Iswaran.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Yes, I believe that all disciplinary cases are of that nature.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Vikram Nair, you have a clarification for Ms Hazel Poa?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I have two clarifications for Ms Hazel Poa.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The first is: does Ms Hazel Poa agree with the presumption of innocence?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And the second is: does Ms Hazel Poa agree that a person who is charged or accused of any wrongdoing should be given a chance to answer that charge and should know the applicable rule before he is charged?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: And Minister Iswaran will be going through the full process of the law to determine whether or not he is guilty or innocent.
